tb21_profile.skill: Localize and repair a subtle memory-corruption regression in a C runtime's allocator/GC data structure, then rebuild a large self-hosting toolchain and run its native testsuite
tb21_profile.domain: OCaml compiler runtime, C systems programming, garbage collection / major-heap free-list management, make-based build of a bootstrapping compiler
tb21_profile.task_form: find-and-patch-a-regression: crash symptom -> root cause in existing source -> rebuild -> verify with the project's own test target

TMax-15K.reason: Crash regression in a C++ repo: bisect to the bad commit, repair a mid-bisect build break, read the core dump, fix, rebuild with make, re-run the test.
Recent commit in a vendored C/C++ library causes an out-of-bounds write; bisect, fix at source, rebuild via Makefile, verify bit-exact against reference.
C undefined behaviour that only bites under -O3 plus a leak of a heap struct; exactly the class of latent memory bug the GC change introduced.
Repairs double-free, dangling-pointer and corruption bugs in a C module with hand-rolled ownership rules, then rebuilds and matches a reference oracle.
Dangling pointers and leaks segfault a C graph evaluator; must fix both the build and the object lifetime discipline, like free-list bookkeeping.
Memory-safety UB in a vendored C library that only crashes at full scale; fix the library itself and rebuild optimised, mirroring a heap bug hidden until bootstrap.
Fix a link error then a memory-safety bug in a custom hash-map's allocation/copy path in C: same allocate-and-track-your-own-storage reasoning.
C source with a build break, an off-by-one corrupting buffers and unbounded recursion; multi-bug C repair under make, though padded with audio/C2 phases.
Make a C interpreter build under -Werror and fix a wrong-result bug in its evaluator core, then drive its test files: same build-then-testsuite loop.
Fix a linker error against a custom C allocation tracker, then minimise the input that triggers the leak and parse the raw heap dump.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Debugging the Pintos kernel under GDB through process loading is the closest this corpus gets to reasoning about a C runtime's internals.
Same Pintos kernel-binary GDB tracing; exercises reading low-level C runtime state rather than application code.
Crashing ARM64 program: trace the fault, fix the source, write the root cause, and automate assemble/link/check targets in a Makefile.
Reproduce the abnormal termination first, then repair the source and re-verify the rebuilt binary; the reproduce-before-fix discipline transfers.
Build a C program from source with debug symbols and use GDB to diagnose its crash; the build-to-debug pipeline matches, the bug is not memory-management.
GDB backtrace and memory inspection of a crashing C binary; analysis only, no fix and no rebuild.
Only real OCaml toolchain practice in the corpus: ocamlbuild/ocamlfind/Makefile driving, useful for the build half, nothing about the runtime.
OCaml QCheck build driven from a project README; teaches reading project docs to learn the build, as HACKING.adoc must be read here.
OCaml/ocamlbuild setup where the sources must be located and a placeholder completed before the build succeeds; toolchain familiarity only.
Must inspect an unfamiliar build system to compile a multi-file C program and write a diagnosis; weak, but the read-the-build-system step is shared.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Segfault from an uninitialised pointer in a C++ library's init path: root-cause why the sentinel is never set and fix it, exactly this task's shape.
Compile a crashing C++ program with debug symbols and drive GDB to the faulting memory access, then explain it; the core debug loop transfers.
LFS cross-binutils first pass: configure and build a toolchain from source with exact flags, the bootstrapping-compiler build half of this task.
Capture and document a SIGSEGV inside radare2's plugin code; native-crash triage in a large C project.
Track a null dereference to a specific line of ln.c under GDB and intervene at runtime: reading C source back from a fault address.
Build with AddressSanitizer and interpret its memory-error report; the sanitizer skill is the fastest route into a heap-corruption bug like this one.
GDB backtrace plus process memory inspection of a crashing binary; diagnosis without a source fix or rebuild.
Compile the Linux kernel from source including modules; same scale of systems build, no debugging component.
Use GDB to inspect internal struct state of a C library from a running process: reading a runtime's live data structures.
Prepare the build environment and compile a large project from source until artifacts appear; only the build-it-from-source half.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: Async generators finalised by the garbage collector misbehave; the closest thing here to reasoning about collection timing and finalisation order.
AutotoolsToolchain mishandles compiler flags after a change; same territory as configuring and building a C project with the right flags.
Compiler-variable resolution broken for cross-building in GnuToolchain; debugging build-toolchain environment logic back from wrong output.
Wrong C++ standard flags emitted for clang and gcc; requires knowing real compiler flag semantics, not just Python.
Deeply nested input blows the recursion depth: reasoning about unbounded recursion over a structure, the stack-overflow failure mode.
Diff parser corrupts its incremental tree state; maintaining a mutated data structure's invariants is the abstract analogue of free-list bookkeeping.
Parallel-build jobs missing from generated CMake presets; build-system plumbing, relevant to driving a big make build but not to the bug.
Inverted condition makes a range-classification loop return wrong blocks or hang; same off-by-one/range-boundary reasoning as run-length block lookup.
Profiler tooling built on a C extension stops instrumenting; adjacent to runtime-instrumentation debugging, but the fix is pure Python plumbing.
Removed serialization methods make every SFTP attribute call fail with one opaque error; practice tracing a generic symptom to the deleted primitive.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Interpreter segfaults during garbage collection after locks are monkeypatched; requires reasoning about runtime object state at collection time.
Compiler emits C where variables are declared outside the block that initialises them, so generated code reads uninitialised memory: compiler-backend C bug.
Compiler lets nested arrays be mutated during iteration; aliasing/lifetime analysis inside a compiler, the same class of invariant violation.
Function calls hoisted to the wrong place in generated C change evaluation order; fixing it means reading emitted C against the source semantics.
C parser and Python parser disagree on transfer encoding and neither is right; debugging across a Cython/C boundary against a reference implementation.
Array-returning calls make the compiler emit references to a variable it never created; tracing bad output code back to the codegen stage.
File-locking flags not propagated to the underlying HDF5 C library; debugging Python-visible behaviour caused by C-level state.
Buzhash seed cancels out for even window sizes, breaking the chunker's invariant; bit-level reasoning about a rolling hash, like run-length block encoding.
Memory-profiler CLI mishandles interpreter startup flags; right domain (allocation tracking) but the bug is argv plumbing, not heap logic.
Type conversion inside an expression crashes the compiler; localising a crash in a compiler pipeline, though a Python-level traceback does the work.

final_top10.reason: Crash regression in a C++ repo: bisect, work around a build break, read the core dump, fix, rebuild with make and re-run the test.
Root-cause a segfault from an uninitialised list-end pointer in a C++ library's init path and fix the initialisation, not the symptom.
A recent commit in a vendored C library causes an out-of-bounds access; bisect, fix at source, rebuild, verify against a reference.
C undefined behaviour that only manifests under -O3 plus an unfreed heap struct: the latent-memory-bug class the GC change introduced.
Fix double-free, corruption and dangling-pointer bugs in C code with hand-rolled ownership rules, then rebuild and match an oracle.
Dangling pointers and leaks segfault a C graph evaluator; must repair both the build and the allocation lifetime discipline.
Memory-safety UB in a vendored C library that only crashes at full scale; fix the library and rebuild optimised.
Rebuild a crashing C++ program with debug symbols and drive GDB to the faulting access; the native-crash debug loop this task needs.
Fix a Makefile link error, then a memory-safety bug in a custom hash map's allocate-and-copy path in C.
Interpreter segfaults during garbage collection after lock objects are patched; reasoning about object state at collection time.

notes: Pool contains only 4 OCaml tasks total (3 RTS QCheck/ocamlbuild builds + tw_226228); none touch the runtime, so OCaml domain match is impossible beyond toolchain familiarity. RTS is the weakest corpus here: ranks 6-10 are padding and 'garbage collection' in RTS is almost entirely `git gc` boilerplate (hundreds of near-duplicate commit-and-pack tasks) - a guaranteed false positive for any lexical retriever on this query. SWE-Smith is pure Python with no memory-management content; its entries are scored on regression-localisation skill only and none should outrank a TMax C crash task. TMax is deep here: I could have filled 20 defensible slots (also considered task_001078_a14d278f, task_009821_3f039f12, task_000696_9e66f3a1, task_009887_3b3d8380). tw_135422 (LFS cross-binutils) is the best match for the bootstrap-the-toolchain half of the task if the merge step wants build coverage.
